sections.lede: I'm Himanshu. For over seven years I've built Android apps that have to talk to other devices, stream video, or keep working when the network drops.
sections.mono: 7+ years of Android · led a team of 5 · worked on Meta and Sony products

sections.title: Making a phone set up a VR headset
body: At Accenture I worked on a Meta tool that lets a phone find, pair and configure AR/VR headsets over Bluetooth, BLE and Wi-Fi Direct. I led the Android side, in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.
more: A lot of the job was chasing connection bugs that only showed up in some regions or on some devices. I dug through ADB and logcat to find the cause, fixed it, and made sure Espresso tests ran in GitHub Actions and GitLab CI before every release. I also reviewed code for a team of 5.
notes: On the side I built the Android part of the Metrolinx travel project.

sections.title: Watch parties that stay in sync
body: At Wipro I worked on a live streaming app for Sony India. I built the watch-party feature, where people on different phones watch the same stream together, and the WebRTC calling that sits on top of the backend APIs.

stats.label: crash rate, after fixing what Crashlytics showed and writing tests first

more: I also made the app work offline with Room and WorkManager, moved some screens to Compose, fixed TalkBack and contrast problems, shrank the app with R8, and handled the Play Store releases.

sections.title: A blockchain side project at work
body: On Sony's Mocopi NFT project I added blockchain-based digital identity to the mobile app.
more: I also cover blockchain basics when I teach, and I hold the Certified Web3 Associate and Certified Hyperledger certificates.

sections.title: An app for insurance agents
body: At Fulcrum Digital I led the Android development of the Al Hilal Mobile Agent App, which agents use for medical and life insurance.
more: I wrote the Kotlin code that keeps policy data in sync while an agent works online, and handled the connection to the backend APIs, which made syncing more reliable.

sections.title: Teaching Android online
body: In 2020 I taught Kotlin and Android live, and wrote the exercises people practised on.

sections.title: Small apps a lot of people used
body: At NetConnect I built and looked after four or more internal Android apps for attendance, asset tracking, billing and day-to-day operations.
more: I connected them to REST APIs, fixed crashes that were hurting people in production, and shipped new features with the backend and product teams.

sections.title: Where it started: Inkpot
body: My first job was at Anytime Softcare in Noida. I built Inkpot there from scratch, an Android app that delivers educational content.

sections.title: The short version
sections.mono: B.Tech Computer Science, Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Technical University, 2016 · Certified Web3 Associate · Certified Hyperledger

sections.title: What I use day to day
Notes
body: I write here about once a month: what I worked on, what went wrong and what I picked up.

sections.title: What I'm reading today
body: Every morning this page pulls in new posts on AI, Android and Kotlin from sources I follow, including Medium. I didn't write them. Each link goes to the original.

sections.title: Need an Android developer?
body: I take freelance and part-time projects, and I'm open to a full-time role with the right team. Send a short note about what you're building and I'll tell you honestly whether I can help.

sections.title: Say hello
body: Email is best. Tell me what you're working on and what you need.
